summary: Cut at 7.0. Round 1 scored 6.0 and round 2 scored 6.5; Caiman is 7 and the ship bar is 7.5. Every gate recorded in the committed JSON is green at export (1536x448): watertight, 0 degenerates, 0 self-crossings on the ring and on all 56 made parts, empty solids and parts notes, 0 vertices in the finger hole, Castable under lost wax with a passed land_widths block (min section 0.900 mm), 0 DFM findings, 1 stone reported and 1 previewed, cold reload identical, 1,770,028 triangles, and the template gate passed at 242,817 of 300,000 bytes. The draft-resolution gates and the zero design.set patch count appear only in the author's report. Round 3 fixed most of the geometry round 2 asked for. The claws are splayed (1.23 and 1.58 mm of skin between feet), they differ in height and reach, and the middle claw curls back 190 deg. The stone has a bed with no daylight under it, the roots are buried 1.05 mm, the papilla stagger is gone, the two coils differ, and the braided, suckered arms and palm curls are the best tentacle work in the collection. The focal point still falls short of 7.5. From the face, each end of the stone is held by a three-fingered hand of smooth, even tubes, and at 300 px the face view still reads as two hands cupping an orb. The claw suckers are ball studs on the tube tops that read as milgrain, not cups. Side-on, the 8.7 x 3.2 mm bed shows as a plain turned drum under the stone. The unfilleted claw roots shear into flat planes where they enter the arms. Both coils read as jump rings or bail loops standing off the shoulders, not as tentacle tips. The author's own score is 7.0, and I agree. This was the last round.
strengths: The braided arms are the ring's signature. There are 6 crossings (theta 15, 38, 143, 166, 204 and 335 deg) with alternating over and under. In reverse.png and shoulder.png they read as separate raised, suckered tentacles, even at 300 px.
The palm curls (palm.png) differ in radius (1.2 / 1.56 / 2.03 / 2.64 mm) and turn count (0.85-1.45), and each carries 8-18 suckers along its inner edge. They read as octopus arm tips, not scrollwork.
The ground is now quiet and correct: papillae at 0.22 / 0.10 mm sit under the 1.44 mm arms, and palm.png shows no straight line of truncated papillae (stagger 0 on both layers).

The claws are now a varied set, not a comb. They stand 3.06 / 5.38 / 3.64 mm over the girdle, reach 1.0 / 1.8 / 1.5 mm, and the middle claw curls back 190 deg. side.png shows the curled pair as a distinctive crest above the stone.
The stone sits on a real bed: side.png shows no daylight between the cabochon's back and the metal, and metal_inside_stone is 0.
The castings are clean: every land-width section is at or above 0.9 mm, the tip balls are 0.936-1.231 mm, and every part has 0 self-crossings.
The template is lean: 242,817 bytes, procedural, with an explicit allowlist (US size, Tentacle height). The author gives reasons for withholding flare and stone size.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Everything is cephalopod: claws grow from the arms, the arms are braided and suckered, the ground is papillae, and the palm curls and shoulder coils carry suckers. Nothing foreign intrudes.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines (stamps, parts or relief), no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: The claws, coils, suckers and bed are CAD parts, and the arms and papillae are analytic curve and tiling layers. Nothing is painted. The arm flanks show no comb fringe in side.png or shoulder.png. The flat planes at the claw roots are a CAD-form defect, scored under the CAD item, not an outline defect.

checklist.item: Faces and eyes read well (a poor face is a defect)
checklist.reason: The ring has no face or eye.

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: The labradorite is fully visible, held by six made claws with gaps of 0.110-0.115 mm, and it rests on a made bed with no daylight in side.png. There are two caveats. All six hooks close over the +x half of the dome (the author says so), so the -x half is held only by flank contacts. The bed shows as a turned drum side-on (see punch item 2).

checklist.item: Shoulder ornament is not cut off toward the face
checklist.reason: The arms run unbroken from the palm curls through the braid into the claw feet. Nothing stops in a wall toward the face.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: (1) Every claw and coil joins unfilleted (the 0.3 mm blend was abandoned), and the buried sweeps shear into flat planar facets where they leave the arms: stones.png x 1180-1260, y 880-1040 and x 430-520, y 900-1060; hero.png x 860-900, y 610-720. (2) The bed is a 3.2 mm-tall straight-walled cylinder, visible side-on as a turned drum: side.png x 620-980, y 400-440; reverse.png x 390-440, y 620-960. (3) The claws are constant-taper smooth tubes (2.0 -> 0.9 mm) ending in 0.936 mm balls, and their 'suckers' are spheres standing proud on top, like beads on a wire (stones.png x 940-1200, y 380-750).

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: This does not apply in full: the base is procedural (Keyframes D-shape, not factory stock). The bore edges and side-face walls stay crisp in side.png and reverse.png.

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Bestiarium rings
checklist.reason: Side-on, the curled claw pair above the stone and the coils standing off both shoulders are unlike Arachne, Manticora, Fenrir, Corvus or Basiliscus. There is a caveat: from the face, three-claw grips cupping a round stone still overlap Harpyia's talon idiom.

checklist.item: Reads as its subject at a glance at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: On contact-300.png the shoulder and reverse views read as tentacles, thanks to the braided, suckered arms. The views that carry the stone do not. In the face view (top middle) two symmetrical three-fingered hands cup an orb. In the side view (top right) antenna-like curled claws stand over a drum, and two round loops hang off the shoulders like bails. The hero reads as 'claws on a cabochon', and the kraken only shows on the right shoulder.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The large forms are the stone, the claw crest and the coils; the medium forms are the braided arms and palm curls; the small forms are the suckers and two papilla scales. Density matches or beats Caiman on the shoulders and palm. It thins on the crown beside the stone (hero.png x 520-860, y 760-880 is near-bare skin) and on the palm crown (palm.png x 560-880, y 540-640), which is lightly hammered.

report.json degenerate_faces 0 and mesh.json quality.degenerate_faces 0 at export (min angle 0.00089 deg, worst aspect 64,346, both flagged as slivers but not counted as degenerate). The draft figure is only in the author's report.

gates.verified: mesh_self_crossings 0. made_parts lists 56 entries (the stone plus 55 CAD parts), and every count is 0 (sum 0). pattern-report.json self_crossings 0.

Every section under 0.8 mm is therefore absent. Caveat: the same block's details list the sucker lips at 0.116-0.129 mm on the 0.45-0.5 mm suckers, under its own detail_floor_mm 0.15, and exceptions does not name them. This is a detail-floor matter, not a section gate, and it is recorded in punch item 6. The sand gates (ray release, clamp bite) do not apply.

previous_punch_items.status: closed in round 2 (verified by the round 2 review), except #9, which round 2 carried forward as its #7

previous_punch_items.from: r2 #1 claws: splay, vary, curl, suckers
previous_punch_items.reason: Skin between feet is 1.23 / 1.58 mm (at least 1.0: met). Heights (3.06 / 5.38 / 3.64) and reaches (1.0 / 1.8 / 1.5) vary: met. The middle claw curls 190 deg: met. There are 3 suckers per claw: met in count, but they read as proud beads, not cups. The outer bearings are -28/+30, not ±34: missed. The acceptance test 'reads as tentacles wrapped round a stone, not as a hand' at 300 px fails in the face view.
No daylight in side.png: met. Bed hidden in face.png: met. Skirt fading over at least 1 mm: missed (0.55 mm fillet). The drum wall shows side-on.

previous_punch_items.from: r2 #3 buried roots and 0.3 mm blend
previous_punch_items.reason: Roots are buried 1.05 mm with the start faces 0.54-0.61 mm under the band: met. The blend was not done, and flat planar faces remain at the claw roots (stones.png x 1180-1260, y 880-1040): the acceptance test fails.
Stagger is 0 on both layers, and palm.png shows no straight line of truncated papillae.

The coils differ (440 vs 360 deg, lengths 43% apart), tighten (2.0 -> 0.95 and 1.75 -> 0.9 mm), carry 5 suckers each, and stand 2.12 / 2.44 mm proud at export: met. But side.png shows two round loops that read as bails or jump rings, and coil A reads as a hook from the hero camera (the author says so).
Papillae are at 0.22 / 0.10 mm, and the arms read as raised braids at 300 px.
US size and Tentacle height are exposed with 0 patches and identical export geometry. Flare, band and stone size are withheld with reasons.

punch_list.zone: Head, theta 60-120 deg: CAD parts 'Claw, rising left / rising / rising right' and the reflected 'Claws, falling hand'
punch_list.change: Break the hand read. Replace the constant-taper round tubes (2.0 -> 0.9 mm) with tentacle sections: an oval section 1.3:1, flattened on the sucker side and widening 15-20% at mid-length before tapering. Add a 20-40 deg twist along each claw so the sucker face rolls from the stone side at the root toward the viewer at the tip. Drop the tip balls in favour of a tapered 0.9 mm domed end. Break the mirror symmetry: rotate the falling hand's bearings 8-12 deg relative to the rising hand, so the two sides of face.png are not reflections.
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png the left and right claw groups are not mirror images; no two claws share a section outline; and no claw ends in a visible sphere. On contact-300.png an unbriefed viewer calls the face view 'tentacles', not 'hands' or 'fingers'. Land widths stay at or above 0.8 mm.

punch_list.zone: CAD part 'Bed' (cylinder 8.7 x 3.2 mm) under the stone at theta 90 deg
punch_list.change: Hide the drum. Either lower the stone 1.5-2.0 mm so the bed's wall is no taller than 1.2 mm, or replace the cylinder with a mantle mound: a domed body swept from the crown, whose side wall falls at 35-50 deg and blends with a fillet of at least 1.0 mm into the crown and the claw feet. Cover its visible wall with the Fine papillae layer.
punch_list.acceptance: In side.png (x 600-1000, y 380-460) and reverse.png (x 380-450, y 600-980) no vertical cylindrical wall or crisp circular edge shows under the stone. There is still no daylight between the stone and the metal, and metal_inside_stone stays 0.

punch_list.zone: Claw roots at the six feet (theta 57-65 and 115-123 deg, v 2.0-6.2 mm) and the two coil roots at theta 27 and 153 deg
punch_list.change: Remove the sheared planes. The 0.3 mm blend failed where the seams cross the arms' creases. Move each claw's start 0.6-0.8 mm along the arm so its seam lands on the arm's crown, not in a crease, then blend at 0.3 mm. If the notes persist, grow the claw from the arm curve layer itself: extend the layer's last points up the claw path so the layer's height field carries the transition, and start the CAD sweep 2 mm up the claw.
punch_list.acceptance: 4x crops of stones.png at x 1180-1260, y 880-1040 and x 430-520, y 900-1060, and of hero.png at x 860-900, y 610-720, show a continuous curvature transition with no flat facet or crisp edge. solids and parts notes stay empty, and self-crossings stay 0.

punch_list.zone: Claw suckers ('Claw, * sucker 1-3' and dimples) on all six claws
punch_list.change: Turn the studs into suckers. Sink each sphere so no more than 35% of its diameter stands proud, move the row onto the claw's inner, stone-facing flank (rolled 60-90 deg from the top), and widen the dimple to 0.55x the diameter, so each sucker reads as a cup rim. Carry 5, not 3, graded 0.7 -> 0.45 mm to the tip.
punch_list.acceptance: In a 2x crop of stones.png at x 940-1200, y 380-750, each sucker shows a dark dimple centre and a rim, not a specular ball. No sucker sits on the claw's top ridge. Every lip is at least 0.15 mm (see item 6).

punch_list.zone: Shoulder coils 'right high tip coil' (theta 27) and 'left low tip coil' (theta 153)
punch_list.change: Stop the loops reading as bails. Keep the neck but lie each coil down onto the band. Lower the lean from -38 deg to -10 to -15 deg so the coil's plane is within 20 deg of the band surface, and let the last half-turn rest on the arm below, touching it. Taper the section continuously to 0.9 mm with no joint sphere ('tip joint' 1.16-1.23 mm).
punch_list.acceptance: In side.png no coil shows an open ring of background at least 0.5 mm across standing clear of the band (today: x 215-330, y 370-470 and x 1195-1370, y 520-620). In hero.png coil A reads as a curled tentacle tip, not a hook. Both tips stay at least 2 mm proud, and land widths stay at or above 0.8 mm.

punch_list.zone: land_widths.details: suckers of 0.45-0.5 mm on the claws and coils
punch_list.change: Either grow the smallest suckers to at least 0.56 mm with the dimple at 0.48x the diameter, so the lip is at least 0.15 mm, or name each lip under 0.15 mm in land_widths.exceptions with its bench treatment (for example, 'lip will cast soft; recut with a 0.3 mm ball graver after casting').
punch_list.acceptance: report.json land_widths.details has no lip_mm under detail_floor_mm 0.15, or each such entry appears in exceptions with a bench note. gates_passed stays true.

punch_list.zone: Grip, dome -x half (theta 90 deg, bearings 180-360 deg in the head plan)
punch_list.change: Balance the grip. At least two of the six hook ends should close over the -x half of the dome, for example the falling hand's middle curl, reflected across the stone's y axis rather than its x axis.
punch_list.acceptance: Each dome half carries at least two tip contacts in the head plan, and face.png shows claws closing over both halves of the stone.

punch_list.zone: Crown beside the stone (hero.png x 520-860, y 760-880) and the palm crown (palm.png x 560-880, y 540-640)
punch_list.change: Carry a third, shorter arm segment or a line of 0.3-0.4 mm papillae across these near-bare patches so density holds at Caiman's level all round.
punch_list.acceptance: No bare patch larger than 3 x 3 mm shows in hero.png or palm.png. DFM stays 0.
